prompt:
Generate one full-fidelity desktop website Privacy page for The Lobby, landscape 3:2, edge to edge, crisp readable text, no browser or device frame. This is a calm document people read to understand their information, not a marketing page.

Activity-led structure: compact masthead “The Lobby” and ordinary “Back to The Lobby” link; title “Privacy”; opening “How The Lobby uses information when you visit, sign in, and use its Tools.” Then three clearly headed reading sections in a single comfortable column:
“When you visit” — “The Schedule Downloader is open without signing in.”
“When you sign in” — “We keep your email address, Tool access, and a sign-in session so you can return to your Tools. The sign-in cookie lasts up to 90 days and renews while you use the site.” Follow with “Members can save teams and use a replaceable private calendar link.”
“When you connect a calendar” — “Google asks for permission to view and edit events across your calendars. The Lobby changes only events it adds in the calendar you choose.” Follow with “You can replace your Member link or disconnect your calendar. Disconnecting removes upcoming games The Lobby added; played games stay.”
Finish with “Running the site” — “AWS and Cloudflare help run and protect The Lobby. Basic service logs and counts of calendar use help keep it working.” Then “Leaving The Lobby” — “Removing membership deletes the access record and Remembered teams.” Quiet footer with a tiny decorative existing robot.

The reference supplies the Local Co-op seafoam/navy palette, Rubik headings, Nunito Sans prose, and flat navy linework; its welcome-page composition does not carry over. Use pale seafoam reading ground, generous legible text, thin rules, and restrained saturated seafoam masthead. No sun, foliage, wave, grain, hero button, cards around paragraphs, fabricated dates, contacts, or settings.
